title: 1996 AHSME Problem 9
statement: Triangle \(PAB\) and square \(ABCD\) are in perpendicular planes. Given that \(PA=3,\) \(PB=4,\) and \(AB=5,\) what is \(PD?\)

solutions.text: Since \(PA^2+PB^2\) \(=3^2+4^2=5^2=AB^2,\) triangle \(PAB\) is right at \(P.\) In square \(ABCD,\) \(AD=5\) and \(AD\perp AB.\) Because the two planes are perpendicular along \(AB,\) \(AD\) is perpendicular to the plane of \(PAB,\) and hence to \(AP.\) Thus \(PD^2=PA^2+AD^2\) \(=3^2+5^2=34.\) The correct answer is B.
hints: First identify the right angle in the \(3\)-\(4\)-\(5\) triangle \(PAB\)
A line in one plane perpendicular to the planes’ intersection is perpendicular to the other plane
